title: Chorister — Formant Singing Studio
description: Drag a vowel plane to make a voice sing, write lyrics onto a step grid, stack four parts, export the choir as a WAV.
concept: A singing-synthesis workbench built on formant tables instead of samples: a band-limited glottal pulse runs through four parallel band-pass resonators whose centre frequencies are the vowel. The Vowel Lab plots the F1/F2 plane so you can drag between a, e, i, o and u — and through the vowels in between that have no name — while a drone morphs under your finger. The Sequencer turns typed lyrics into sung syllables, synthesising consonants too: p/t/k snap, s/f/h hiss, m/n hum into the note, and a trailing nasal closes it. The Choir stacks four parts with their own voice type, octave, detune spread and stagger, and the whole thing renders offline to a peak-normalised WAV.
features: Vowel Lab: drag the F1/F2 formant plane to morph a live drone continuously between vowels
16-step, 8-row sequencer with five scales, selectable root, gate and tempo
Lyric-to-syllable engine that synthesises consonant onsets and nasal codas
Four-part choir with per-part voice type, octave, level, detune spread, stagger and pan
Live formant-response plot showing the resonance envelope against the pitch's harmonics
Five presets, an improviser, and a procedural convolution reverb
Offline render to a peak-normalised 16-bit stereo WAV download
Song saved to localStorage, packed into a share link, or exported as JSON

interaction.mouse: Drag the vowel plane to sing and morph formants; drag sliders to reshape the voice.
interaction.click: Tap grid cells to place notes, tap a choir part to edit it, tap a preset to load one.
interaction.touch: The vowel plane, the grid and every control are pointer-driven and work on touch.
interaction.keyboard: 1–8 pick a scale degree and sing it, space starts and stops the transport.
